papers.title_in_file: Amazon Braket supported regions and devices - Amazon Braket
papers.version_note: A web documentation page (HTML text layer, no page breaks); undated in the text, so every listing is a snapshot as read.
papers.what_it_is: An Amazon Braket Developer Guide page listing the QPU and simulator devices, their ARNs and regions, and the AWS regions and endpoints where Braket is available.

assertions.value: The page states that Amazon Braket provides access to QPU devices from AQT, IonQ, IQM, QuEra, and Rigetti.
quotes: Amazon Braket provides access to QPU devices from AQT, IonQ, IQM, QuEra, and Rigetti.
assertions.certainty_reason: Amazon describes its own service in its own developer documentation.

assertions.value: The page states that AWS offers access to on-demand, local, and embedded simulators.
quotes: Additionally, AWS offers access to on-demand, local, and embedded simulators.
assertions.certainty_reason: Amazon describes its own service in its own developer documentation.

assertions.value: The page defines a device in Amazon Braket as a quantum processing unit (QPU) or simulator that you can call to run quantum tasks.
quotes: In Amazon Braket, a device represents a quantum processing unit (QPU) or simulator that you can call to run quantum tasks.
assertions.certainty_reason: Amazon describes its own service in its own developer documentation.

assertions.value: The page states that device ARNs are case sensitive and gives the example that the AQT IBEX-Q1 ARN must contain 'Ibex-Q1'.
assertions.anchor: Device and region page, note after device table
quotes: Note Device ARNs are case sensitive. For example, when using the AQT IBEX-Q1 device, verify that the device ARN contains 'Ibex-Q1'.
assertions.certainty_reason: Amazon describes its own service in its own developer documentation.

assertions.value: The page states that device properties such as device topology, calibration data, and native gate sets are available on the Devices tab of the Amazon Braket console or by the GetDevice API.
assertions.anchor: Device and region page, Device properties
quotes: For all devices, you can find further device properties, such as device topology, calibration data, and native gate sets, on the Devices tab of the Amazon Braket console or by the GetDevice API.
assertions.certainty_reason: Amazon describes its own service in its own developer documentation.

assertions.value: The page states that when constructing a circuit with the simulators, Amazon Braket requires contiguous qubits or indices.
assertions.anchor: Device and region page, Device properties
quotes: When constructing a circuit with the simulators, Amazon Braket requires that you use contiguous qubits or indices.
assertions.certainty_reason: Amazon describes its own service in its own developer documentation.

assertions.value: The page states that quantum tasks on a QPU are viewed in the console in the Region of that device, and that the SDK can submit tasks to any QPU device regardless of working Region by automatically creating a session to the Region of the specified QPU.
assertions.anchor: Device and region page, Regions and endpoints
quotes: Quantum tasks that run on a QPU device can be viewed in the Amazon Braket console in the Region of that device.
When using the Amazon Braket SDK, you can submit quantum tasks to any QPU device, regardless of the Region in which you are working.
The SDK automatically creates a session to the Region for the QPU specified.
assertions.certainty_reason: Amazon describes its own service in its own developer documentation.
